@[expose] public section

-- TODO(mercuris): define a recursive version of this for better usability?
-- TODO(mercuris): add `Real.iteratedLogb` for general bases
/-- The iterated logarithm of `x` is the number of times the natural logarithm
must be iteratively applied before the result is less than or equal to `1`.
Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterated_logarithm -/
noncomputable def Real.iteratedLog (x : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sInf { (n : ℕ) | Real.log^[n] x ≤ 1 }

theorem Real.iteratedLog_eq_zero_of_le {x : ℝ} (hx : x ≤ 1) :
    Real.iteratedLog x = 0 := by
  simpa [iteratedLog] using Or.inl hx

theorem Real.iteratedLog_eq_zero_of_neg {x : ℝ} (hx : x < 0) :
    Real.iteratedLog x = 0 :=
  Real.iteratedLog_eq_zero_of_le (by linarith)

theorem iteratedLog_two : Real.iteratedLog 2 = 1 := by
  simp [Real.iteratedLog]
  have : Real.log 2 ≤ 1 := by
    convert Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (show 0 < 2 by norm_num)
    norm_num
  rw [Nat.sInf_def ⟨1, this⟩]
  exact (Nat.find_eq_iff _).2 ⟨this, fun n hn => by simp [Nat.lt_one_iff.1 hn]⟩

theorem iteratedLog_four : Real.iteratedLog 4 = 2 := by
  simp [Real.iteratedLog]
  have : Real.log^[2] 4 ≤ 1 := by
    have h_ne_zero : Real.log √4 ≠ 0 := by simp; linarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg 4]
    have : Real.log 4 ≤ 2 := by
      have := mul_eq_of_eq_mul_inv₀ h_ne_zero <| div_eq_mul_inv _ (2 : ℝ) ▸ (Real.log_sqrt (show 0 ≤ 4 by linarith))
      rw [← this]
      norm_num
      convert! Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (show 0 < 2 by norm_num)
      norm_num
    have : Real.log 4 - 1 ≤ 1 := by convert sub_le_sub_right this 1; norm_num
    exact le_trans (Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (Real.log_pos <| by norm_num)) this
  rw [Nat.sInf_def ⟨2, by aesop⟩]
  refine (Nat.find_eq_iff _).2 ⟨by aesop, fun n hn => ?_⟩
  interval_cases n; simp
  simp [Real.lt_log_iff_exp_lt]
  linarith [Real.exp_one_lt_d9]

findings.description: Direct consumer in FormalConjectures/Arxiv/1609.08688/sIncreasingrTuples.lean:230–232. The norm-based condition `(fun n => (Real.iteratedLog n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] Ω` is used as if it asserted a positive lower bound on Ω. It also permits `Ω n := -(Real.iteratedLog n : ℝ)`, with big-O constant 1. Since this gives `Real.exp (Ω n) ≤ 1`, the entire declaration follows from the elementary bound `maximalLength_le`, without any logarithmic saving. This derivation was checked in Lean without sorry. The same formal schema admits F(n) = n², which was separately proved not to satisfy the source's positive exponential saving.
findings.source_evidence: Gowers–Long, https://arxiv.org/e-print/1609.08688 (v2), §1.1, Proposition 1.6, states `F(n) ≤ n² / exp(Ω(log*(n)))`. Its proof explicitly obtains an o(n²) bound from triangle removal and then invokes Fox's quantitative bound. This requires an eventually positive exponent bounded below by a positive multiple of log*. Mathlib Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean, `isBigO_iff` and `isBigO_neg_right`, confirms that the Lean big-O condition instead controls absolute values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(∀ᶠ n in atTop, 0 ≤ Ω n)` to the witness conditions. Together with the existing big-O condition, this is equivalent to `∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c * (Real.iteratedLog n : ℝ) ≤ Ω n`, restoring the intended positive exponential saving. This equivalence was checked in `/workspace/review/consumer_fix_scratch.lean`.

status_issues.source_status: The covering variant was proved affirmatively by L. Pyber in 1985: every n-vertex graph can have its edges covered by n−1 cycles and edges. The cited paper identifies the reference as “An Erdős–Gallai conjecture”, Combinatorica 5(1), 67–79 (1985).
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2211.07689 (v2), introduction, “Covering problems”: “In 1985, Pyber ... proved the covering version of the Erdős-Gallai conjecture, showing that the edges of any n-vertex graph can be covered with n−1 cycles and edges.”
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved`, replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`, and add the Pyber reference.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses a conditional infimum over natural-number iteration counts instead of the reference's recursive stopping rule.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The defining set is nonempty for every real input: until an iterate is at most 1, its value is positive and taking a logarithm decreases it by at least 1. Thus the natural-number infimum is the genuine minimum, never the empty-set default. In `/workspace/review/scratch_with_uniqueness.lean`, I proved both the first-stopping-time characterization and the exact equivalence `(∀ x, F x = if x ≤ 1 then 0 else 1 + F (Real.log x)) ↔ F = Real.iteratedLog`. Nonpositive inputs stop at iteration zero, so Mathlib's extended logarithm values do not change the result.

reformulations.difference: Bucić–Montgomery explicitly use base-2 logarithms, whereas Real.iteratedLog uses natural logarithms. These counts differ pointwise, but the consumer uses them only inside a big-O bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For the binary first-stopping count L₂ and the library count Lₑ, Lean proves `Lₑ(x) ≤ L₂(x) ≤ Lₑ(x) + 2`. For natural n ≥ 2, Lₑ(n) ≥ 1, hence L₂(n) ≤ 3 Lₑ(n). Consequently n Lₑ(n) and n L₂(n) have the same big-O bounds. `/workspace/review/base_scratch.lean` proves, for arbitrary f : ℕ → ℝ, the exact equivalence `f =O[atTop] (fun n => n * Lₑ(n)) ↔ f =O[atTop] (fun n => n * L₂(n))`. All other conjuncts of the consumer are unchanged. Empty and one-vertex graph cases were also checked.
